newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian sugar firm on limited supply, business slow.
newsitem.headline: Indian sugar firm on limited supply, business slow.

text.p: Sugar prices turned firm on Thursday on a shortage of ready stock but consumer offtake remained typically slow for the end of the month, dealers said.
Ready delivery sugar S-30 rose by 5-9 rupees to 1,480/1,500 per quintal while sugar M-30 rose 10 rupees to 1,500/1,535.
"Speculative buying on expectations of higher festival demand in the coming days as well as restricted offerings...aided the firm tendency," one broker said.
Mill delivery sugar remained unquoted as local millers have already sold out their allotted quantity of sugar from the free sale quota for July.
"Thin offerings by the millers had curtailed inflow of sugar from mills to the market and resulted in a shortage of ready stock in the Bombay market," he said.
"I am expecting higher offtake in the coming days ahead of festivals, and prices may remain firm looking at the lower free sale quota," he said.

He said the free sale quota for July was 750,000 tonnes against 800,000 tonnes released for June, while the quota of 750,000 tonnes for August would not be sufficient for the seasonal festival demand.
